export_future_stack_control.change: Heap-allocate the transient child interpreter in call_harn_export_by_name so composing futures retain a pointer rather than the interpreter inline.
limitations: The before census is from the pull request's Linux CI job; the after census is from an owned Linux host with the same pinned compiler and collection command. This is a stack-budget regression check, not a controlled runtime or CI latency trial.
Two existing budgets follow the interpreter files into harn-vm-core without changing their byte limits. No budget was increased.

library_build_trial.target_isolation: Separate initially empty targets, sequential capacity-leased builds, one shared pinned Kache 1.2.1 object store with private runtime directories.
limitations: One observation per source, in that order, on a shared host. This is not a controlled latency distribution.
The first arm primed unchanged dependencies for the second, as the unequal cache counters show. The package-wall difference cannot be attributed solely to extraction.

Cargo's native library unit fell by 12.38 seconds in this sample; the new core unit took 12.26 seconds and pipelined with the native unit. These are full compilation-unit durations, not isolated frontend timings.
The command includes harn-test-echo-env; it does not build the shared CLI producer or compile the test units.
The latest recorded merge-queue p90 remains 1225 seconds against the 600-second goal.

test_unit_rebuild_trial.method: Alternate native/core twice, retain built third-party dependencies in each private target, touch only each workspace library entry file to force recompilation without changing its contents, and verify clean Git status before and after each sample. Cargo timings confirm the native test unit compiled in every sample and both core units compiled in each after sample.
limitations: Two observations per source on a shared host are not a CI latency distribution or isolated frontend measurements.
This compiles test binaries without running tests or building the shared CLI producer. Existing dependencies and filesystem caches are warm.

The first attempted core control failed because cached metadata was read-only. Only that private target's core/native dev artifacts were cleaned before the recorded successful core samples; no cached hardlink was made writable.
The earlier cache-enabled test attempt failed on two Linux-only private-field callers; the successful corrected retry reused dependencies and is excluded from this comparison.
The modest total-wall difference does not establish that the 600-second merge-queue goal has been met; the latest recorded p90 remains 1225 seconds.

generator_runtime_control.conclusion: The repeated control does not establish a runtime speedup or regression. Earlier slower measurements of the same control artifact do not establish an extraction benefit.
limitations: The control artifact's source revision is unavailable and its version differs, so this is an artifact comparison, not a source-isolated causal experiment.
The samples are sequential on a shared developer host and do not establish a production performance distribution.
